message.content:
Below is a **complete `curl`‑based REST API call** that creates a new Compute Engine VM in Google Cloud Platform (GCP), attaches one NVIDIA RTX A6000–equivalent accelerator (the closest supported type is *NVIDIA A100* – see note below), boots from an Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image, and sets all required fields explicitly so you can copy/paste into your own script.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Create a GCE instance named “rtx-a6000-demo” in zone us-central1-b
# with:
#   • Machine type : n1-highmem-16 (adjust per your workload)
#   • Accelerator  : 1 × NVIDIA A100 (closest match to RTX A6000)
#   • Boot disk    : Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (focal)
#   • Network      : Default VPC + subnet
#   • Metadata     : SSH key & startup‑script placeholder
#

PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-b"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo"

# OAuth token obtained via gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

cat <<EOF > /tmp/create_instance.json
{
  "kind": "compute#regionInstance",
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "description": "Demo instance with NVIDIA RTX A6000 equivalent.",
  "tags": {
    "items": ["default-tag"]
  },
  "labels": {
    "env":"demo","purpose":"test"
  },

  # ---------- MACHINE TYPE ----------
  "machineType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-highmem-16",

  # ---------- BOOT DISK ----------
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "diskSizeGb": 50,
        "sourceImage": "projects/canonical-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],

  # ---------- NETWORK INTERFACE ----------
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "subnetworks": [],
      "accessConfigs": [ { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"} ]
    }
  ],

  # ---------- ACCELERATOR ----------
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/types/nvidia-a100"
    }
  ],

  # ---------- METADATA ----------
  "metadata": {
    "fingerprint": "",
    "items": [
      {"key":"ssh-keys","value":"${USER}:${SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_CONTENTS}\n"},
      {"key":"startup-script","value":"echo \"Hello World\" >> /var/log/startup.log"}
    ]
  },

  # ---------- SCHEDULING ----------
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  }

}
EOF

# Execute the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://${COMPUTE_ENDPOINT:-compute.googleapis.com}/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @/tmp/create_instance.json
```

### How it works

| Section | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **Machine Type** | Uses `n1-highmem-16`. Pick another type (`e.g., e2-standard-4`) depending on CPU/RAM requirements. |
| **Boot Disk** | Installs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS from Canonical’s public family image. Adjust size if needed. |
| **Network Interface** | Attaches to the default VPC/subnet and gives external IP. Remove `accessConfigs` for internal only. |
| **Guest Accelerators** | Adds one NVIDIA A100 GPU. Replace `"nvidia-a100"` with `"nvidia-p100"` or other if you prefer. |
| **Metadata** | Inserts SSH keys and a simple startup script. Replace `${SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_CONTENTS}` with your actual public key. |
| **Scheduling** | Enables automatic restart after host maintenance. |

---

#### Why “RTX A6000” isn’t listed?

Google Compute Engine currently offers NVIDIA GPUs under the following names:

| Brand | Model | GCP Name |
|-------|------|----------|
| NVIDIA | RTX A6000 | Not offered directly |
| NVIDIA | A100 | `nvidia-a100` |
| NVIDIA | K80 | `nvidia-k80` |
| ... | … | … |

Because the RTX A6000 is essentially an NVIDIA Ampere‑architecture card, the nearest matching product in GCP is the **NVIDIA A100**. That’s why the above template uses `nvidia-a100`. If you truly need an RTX A6000, you’ll have to check whether GCP has added support since writing this guide—otherwise consider contacting GCP sales or exploring alternative providers that expose RTX A6000 hardware.

--- 

Feel free to tweak the parameters (CPU count, memory, region, etc.) to fit your exact workload!
